subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: If current-main tracing shows scheduled agent work issuing these invalid reads, should OpenClaw change the scheduler/bootstrap producer, or should invalid workspace reads remain ordinary tool-level failures?
rationale: The observed paths are not produced by the inspected cron bootstrap allowlist, and choosing between producer correction and read-tool semantics changes the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Trace before changing behavior
options.body: Require a current-main trace and heap/RSS capture that identifies the request producer, then implement only the owner-boundary correction it proves.

options.title: Harden the read surface
options.body: Add generic handling for invalid read targets, accepting that this may mask invalid scheduled or agent-generated requests without proving the RSS root cause.

recommendation.title: Trace before changing behavior
recommendation.body: Require a current-main trace and heap/RSS capture that identifies the request producer, then implement only the owner-boundary correction it proves.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only identified human who volunteered to investigate this exact report; code ownership remains unproven.
